Consult Summary:
- Adult male with known heart failure presents with 2 weeks of progressively worsening dyspnea (notably worse over the last few days) and new bilateral ankle swelling; exam/vitals reportedly OK; plan made to increase diuretic and arrange labs and echocardiogram.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Progressive shortness of breath.
- Timeline: Gradual onset over “last couple of weeks,” notably worse in the past few days.
- Functional impact: Previously able to walk to the shops; now breathless with minimal exertion and around the house; needs to sit to catch breath.
- Associated symptoms: Mild dry cough; new bilateral ankle swelling over the past few days; feels a bit run-down.
- Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no palpitations, no fever; appetite OK; urinating frequently (attributed to diuretics).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not reported.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic heart failure; previously had dyspnea that improved with medication (diuretic).
- Prior “small heart attack” about 5 years ago; hospitalized for a few days; patient unable to recall exact diagnosis name but states it was “more than angina.”
- No other chronic conditions reported.

Medications:
- Furosemide (dose not recalled; route/frequency not documented). Clinician plans to increase from one tablet daily to one tablet twice daily for a few days.
- Aspirin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Bisoprolol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Lives alone with two cats.
- Part-time lorry (truck) driver; daytime shifts only.
- Former smoker: ~1 pack/day for ~25 years; quit smoking.
- No alcohol use.
- Exercise: Walks to the shops daily.

Family History:
- Father died of a heart attack in his early 60s.
- Mother has osteoporosis and is living.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Oxygen saturation “OK,” blood pressure “OK” (no values provided).
- Chest exam: Described as “OK” by clinician.
- Other exam findings: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- Ordered: Blood tests including complete blood count (to assess for anemia) and kidney function.
- Imaging/Studies: Echocardiogram requested; expected scheduling within 1–2 weeks.
- Results: Not yet available.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Subacute worsening dyspnea in a patient with chronic heart failure, most consistent with an acute decompensation (volume overload), given new bilateral ankle edema and prior response to diuretics, with stable reported vitals/exam.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Acute decompensated chronic heart failure (volume overload): Supported by known HF, progressive exertional dyspnea, new bilateral ankle edema, prior benefit from diuretic; opposed by lack of documented orthopnea/PND and normal-sounding exam/oxygen saturation.
  - Anemia contributing to dyspnea: Supported by feeling run-down and plan for CBC; opposed by absence of bleeding symptoms and edema better explained by HF.
  - Arrhythmia precipitating decompensation: Possible trigger even without palpitations; opposed by patient denying palpitations and clinician stating vitals are OK (no irregularity noted).

- Issue 1: Shortness of breath, likely HF exacerbation.
  - Plan:
    - Increase Furosemide to one tablet twice daily for the first few days (per clinician).
    - Safety net: Call sooner if worsening breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.
    - Follow-up in 1 week to reassess symptoms and response.

- Issue 2: Chronic heart failure—evaluation of current status.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange echocardiogram to assess cardiac function.
    - Reassess clinically after results.

- Issue 3: Possible contributing anemia and/or renal dysfunction.
  - Plan:
    - Obtain CBC and renal function tests; review results at follow-up.

- General plan items:
  - None additional documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital sign values recorded (HR, BP, RR, SpO2 numerically not provided).
  - Limited physical exam details; no documentation of JVP, rales, S3, hepatomegaly, or weight changes.
  - No inquiry documented about orthopnea/PND, recent dietary/salt intake changes, medication adherence, or new OTC NSAID use.
  - Medication doses and exact frequencies not documented.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None noted. Minor clarification: clinician initially misheard beta-blocker as metoprolol; patient confirms bisoprolol.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; occasional connection/audio issues noted by clinician.
